en: Far from Bergson’s assertion that ‘the memory of the present’ coincides with ‘false recognition’ (he uses the terms as synonyms), they are exact opposites. We have already observed that while the ‘memory of the present’ allows for the experience of the possible, ‘false recognition’ instead dissimulates or wipes away this experience. The remembered present is virtual: it is a potential that coexists with the (perceived) act, but is not cancelled out by it. With ‘false recognition’, conversely, the simultaneous presence of heterogeneous moments (the potential and the act) is camouflaged as the chronologically articulated repetition of a homogeneous
; the
‘now’ is passed off as a
-‘back then’; the present event seems like the hallucinatory verbatim copy of another event that took place in some previous period.
zh: 柏格森断言‘对当下的记忆’与‘错误再认’相一致，把二者当作同义词；但实际上，二者恰恰相反。我们已经看到，“对当下的记忆”使可能性经验得以出现，而“错误再认”反而掩饰或抹除这种经验。被记住的当下是潜在的：它是与被知觉的实现共存、却不被后者取消的潜能。反过来，在“错误再认”中，异质环节（潜能与实现）的同时在场，被伪装成同质实现依年代展开的重复；可能的“现在”被冒充为实在的“那时”；当前事件看起来像是先前某个时期发生的另一事件之逐字逐句的幻觉性摹本。

en: In both cases, an
is at work: both the manifestation and concealment of the virtual make use of a
process, postulating the transposition of the
onto the past. And yet here we have two types of anachronism that are not dissimilar, but antithetical: a
(more pretentiously, transcendental) one innervating ‘the memory of the present’; and a

(but also, factual) opposite one corresponding to ‘false recognition’. Here, we can jump forward to the idea that a paralysis of history, as well as the state of mind on which this feeds, traces its origins back to the surreptitious transformation of the formal anachronism into a real anachronism. It traces
its origins, that is, back to the overturning of ‘the memory of the present’ into a ‘false recognition’.
zh: 两种情形中都有时代错置在起作用：潜在态的显现和遮蔽都借助了一个逆时间过程，都设定把此时此地移植到过去。然而，我们面对的并非仅仅相异、而是彼此对立的两种时代错置：一种是贯穿“对当下的记忆”的形式的时代错置（formal anachronism；说得更玄一些，也可称先验的时代错置（transcendental anachronism））；另一种则是与“错误再认”相应的现实的时代错置（real anachronism，也即事实的时代错置）。这里可以提前提出一个观念：历史的瘫痪及其赖以滋长的心境，都源于形式的时代错置被暗中转化为现实的时代错置。换句话说，它们源于“对当下的记忆”翻转成了“错误再认”。

en: The

consists of the application of the past-form to the present that is currently underway. But the past-form (or past-in-general) is nothing other than language, a faculty, a disposition. This being so, to apply the past-form to the present means to understand the word being uttered as an index of, or testament to, linguistic competence; to spot in a specific performance the disposition or capacity that allows for it; to push the act taking place back within its correlated
; to catch sight of what is loveable in the loved. When the events now being experienced are inserted anachronistically into the faculty – into the

they are, as well as being real, always also potential. Bergson’s thesis that ‘a representation can bear the mark of the past independently of what it represents’ could be paraphrased as follows: we can grasp an anachronistic ‘before’ in any given experience, and this ‘before’ is a disposition (the capacity-to-speak, capacity-to-enjoy, etc.). A representation ‘bears the mark of the past’ whenever the represented fact lets its own condition of possibility seep through. The formal anachronism allows the present to be considered from the prospective angle of the faculty; but not only the present. The past-in-general – that is, the inexhaustible potential of language or the intellect – equally regards both events that took place long ago (as we already know, in such a case we ought speak of a
), and events that are still to come (that is, in the
). The temporality of potential – namely, the formal anachronism – intersects the linear, chronological succession of time at every point, complicating and dilating it.
zh: 形式的时代错置，就是把过去形式应用于正在展开的当下。但过去形式（或一般过去）无非就是语言、官能或禀赋。因此，把过去形式应用于当下，意味着把正在说出的词理解为语言能力的指标或见证；意味着在某项具体表现中看出使其成为可能的禀赋或能力；意味着把正在发生的实现推回与它相关的潜能（dynamis）；意味着在所爱之物中瞥见使它值得被爱的东西。当前经历的事件一旦以时代错置的方式被嵌入官能、嵌入“不定的过去”，便不仅是实在的，而且始终也是潜在的。柏格森断言“一个表象可以带有过去的标记，而与它所表象的内容无关”；这个命题可以改述如下：我们能在任何经验中把握一个时代错置的“之前”，而这个“之前”就是一种禀赋（言说能力、享受能力，等等）。每当被表象的事实使其自身的可能性条件从中渗出时，一个表象便“带有过去的标记”。形式的时代错置使我们能够从官能的视角考察当下；但它所考察的不只是当下。一般过去——即语言或智力不可穷尽的潜能——同样关涉久远以前发生的事件（我们已经知道，此时应当说过去的过去）以及尚未到来的事件（即未来的过去）。潜能的时间性——也就是形式的时代错置——在每一点上与线性、年代性的时间接续相交，使后者变得复杂并得到扩展。

en: The memory of the present demonstrates both the inextricable mutual belonging of a faculty and a determinate execution of it,
the ‘difference of nature’ that makes it impossible to reduce the one to the other. I say
because while a memory does, indeed, come into being, it is a memory ‘of the present’, of the very same present that is simultaneously perceived. Though the

bifurcates – into language and the word that is spoken, enjoyment and the capacity to enjoy, a specific understanding of something and intellectual potential in general – it is an immediate and single whole. I say

because while what is at question here is, indeed, the present, we also have a ‘memory’ of it. The disposition’s capacity-to-be, appearing as an elusive ‘back then’, is always distinguished on each occasion from the actually-realised action (even though it has an iron relation of unity with it). But what, ultimately, does the memory of the present reveal, when it exhibits the concomitance – and yet also the difference – between a faculty and its performance? Nothing less than the (not-usually-apparent) genesis of
; or, if we prefer, the fundamental condition on the basis of which the process of the reproduction of life breaks out of a predetermined and invariant pattern of behaviour.
zh: 对当下的记忆既表明某种官能与它的一次特定实行不可分割地相互归属，又表明二者之间存在一种使任何一方都不能被还原为另一方的“性质差别”。我说相互归属，是因为这里确实生成了一段记忆，但它是“对当下”的记忆，是对那个同时也被知觉的同一个当下的记忆。此时此地虽然分岔为语言与所说之词、享受与享受能力、对某物的特定理解与一般智力潜能，但它仍是一个直接而单一的整体。我说差别，是因为这里所涉及的固然是当下，但我们同时也对它拥有一段“记忆”。禀赋所包含的存在能力以一个难以捉摸的‘那时’显现，每一次都同实际实现的行动区别开来（尽管二者之间有着牢不可破的统一关系）。那么，对当下的记忆在展示官能与其表现的并存及其差别时，最终揭示了什么？它所揭示的不是别的，正是通常并不显现的历史时间之生成；或者也可以说，是生命再生产过程据以摆脱预定而不变的行为模式的根本条件。

en: The difference between the simultaneous potential ‘now’ and real ‘now’, the present of the faculty and the present of the performance, is the fulcrum of all truly historical experience. It is its fulcrum, but also its wellspring. Such a difference should be imputed to the very
of experience. There is history in language
: even though it is only manifested through determinate acts of speaking, it is never exhausted by this or that particular utterance, nor even by an infinite series of

utterances – rather, it exists as a potential that could never be accomplished. There is history in the fact that a determinate piece of work or a determinate understanding of something is inseparable yet also wholly different from the faculty to which it corresponds, labour-power and the intellect respectively. There is history in the fact that the irreversible flow of ‘now’s incessantly intersects with the perpendicular we call the past-in-general: the single ‘now’, preceded and followed by other specific ‘now’s, itself harbours the temporal (but
chronological) relation between the ‘before’ of a disposition (the
) and the ‘after’ of its realisation.
zh: 同时存在的潜能之“现在”与实在之“现在”之间的差别，也就是官能的当下与实际表现的当下之间的差别，是一切真正历史经验的支点；它既是支点，也是源泉。这样的差别应当归属于经验本身的历史性。语言本身之中就有历史：语言虽然只有通过特定言说活动才会显现，却从不会被这个或那个具体话语耗尽，甚至也不会被无限系列的话语耗尽；它作为一种永远不可能完成的潜能而存在。一项特定劳动或对某物的一次特定理解，分别同其相应的官能——劳动力（labour-power）与智力——既不可分离又完全不同；这一事实之中就有历史。不可逆的一个个“现在”持续流动，同时又不断同我们称为一般过去的垂线相交；这一事实之中也有历史：单个“现在”之前和之后虽然都有其他具体“现在”，但它自身也包含禀赋之“之前”（现在的过去）与其实现之“之后”之间那种属于时间却不属于年代顺序的关系。

en: There would be no history, then, if the instant that I am living through were only perceived, rather than also being remembered as I experience it; if the ‘totality of what we are seeing, hearing and experiencing’ were not at each moment split into ‘actual and virtual, perception on the one side and memory on the other’. The formal anachronism, whose prerogative is to display both the intertwining and the hiatus between the possible and the real, is neither anti-historical nor supra-historical, but, so to speak,

. The difficulties and the dilemmas that this sometimes raises do not in fact depend on any apparent suspension of the genesis of history, but rather – quite the contrary – on the direct, almost empirical and yet dazzling demonstration of what it is that makes this genesis historical.
zh: 因此，如果我正在经历的瞬间只被知觉，而没有在经历之际同时被记住；如果“我们正在看见、听见和经历的一切”并不在每一时刻分裂为“现实态与潜在态，一边是知觉，另一边是记忆”，那么历史就不会存在。形式的时代错置以展示可能与实在之间的交织和断裂为其特性；它既非反历史，也非超历史，而可以说是一种使之历史化的作用。它有时引起的困难和两难，并不取决于历史生成表面上遭到中止；恰恰相反，它们来自对那个使这种生成成为历史生成的东西所作的直接、近乎经验性却又耀眼夺目的展示。

en: The

distorts, inverts and dissembles the processes and results of the formal anachronism. It is a reaction to the formal anachronism, a backlash against or antidote to it, or perhaps an escape-tunnel from it. What is really the splitting of one same
into act and potential is transfigured, through a
diachronic relation, into two identical acts, into two separate
characterised by the same perceptual content. In the real anachronism, the past-
which confers a virtual character on the present – is systematically reduced to a past
, and the present provides a coterminous copy of it. But what does such a reduction entail?
zh: 现实的时代错置歪曲、颠倒并掩饰形式的时代错置之过程及结果。它是对形式的时代错置的一种反应，是针对它的反冲或解毒剂，也可能是一条逃离它的隧道。同一个此时此地原本分裂为实现与潜能，却通过一种历时关系（diachronic relation）被改造为两个完全相同的实现，改造为两个彼此分离却具有同一知觉内容的此时此地。在现实的时代错置中，那个赋予当下以潜在性质的过去形式，被系统地还原成一个过去事实；而当下则为它提供了一个范围完全重合的摹本。然而，这种还原意味着什么？

en: We know that the past-form (or past-in-general) is language, disposition, the condition of possibility. As such, to confuse the past-
for a past
means to conceive the language faculty – the mere capacity-to-speak – as

, the mass of actually-performed utterances. The faculty is equated to a single performance, or better, to the previous performance which appears as the prototype of the one now being performed. The condition of possibility of an event is represented as another event, its outdated original version. The disposition towards pleasure is totally identified with the pleasures already enjoyed, the intellect coincides with a series of particular understandings, labour-power becomes indistinguishable from labour that has been carried out, and only the already-loved is loveable. The real anachronism denies the
of potential and act, disposition and performance, past-in-general and instantaneous present; but, for precisely this reason, it also denies their essential

. Language, equated to an utterance that has already been uttered, can no longer be said to be simultaneous to the utterance that is being uttered now. Besides, and for the same reason – because it is assimilated to a (past) act of speaking – language appears coextensive or indeed entirely homogeneous with the act of speaking realised in a certain present moment. As such, it is impossible to see difference
between the two accomplished facts, between the two performances. If there is a difference, it is one of degree,
nature.
zh: 我们知道，过去形式（或一般过去）就是语言、禀赋和可能性条件。因此，把过去形式误认成过去事实，就意味着把语言官能——单纯的言说能力——理解为已经说出的词，理解为实际产生过的全部话语。官能被等同于一次具体表现；更准确地说，被等同于那次较早的表现，而后者看起来仿佛是当前表现的原型。一个事件的可能性条件被表象成另一个事件，成为它属于过去的原始版本。享受快感的禀赋被完全等同于已经享受过的快感；智力与一系列特定理解重合；劳动力同已经完成的劳动无法区分；只有已经被爱过的东西才值得爱。现实的时代错置否认潜能与实现、禀赋与表现、一般过去与瞬时当下同时存在；但也正因为如此，它同时否认它们之间的本质差别。语言一旦被等同于已经说过的话语，就不能再被说成与此刻正在说出的话语同时存在。此外，也出于同一原因——因为语言被同化成了一项过去的言说实现——它便显得同某个当前时刻实现的言说活动范围一致，甚至完全同质。如此一来，我们不可能在两个已经完成的事实、两次实际表现之间看出差别。即便存在差别，那也只是程度而非性质上的差别。

en: ‘False recognition’ closes the hiatus between potential and act, a hiatus fully brought into focus by the memory of the present. It identifies a faculty with the sum of its objectifications. It reabsorbs the past-in-general back into the chronological sequence of time. But the enduring discrepancy between potential and act, language and the word spoken, labour-power and a specific labour (a discrepancy which strikes us in conjunction with their simultaneity and mutual belonging) is the matrix of historical time. As such, ‘false recognition’ masks the historicity of experience. The real anachronism
. That is to say, it induces the state of mind based on which people are led to conclude that history is now exhausted, that ‘there is never anything new … each moment [is] a repetition of the past’.
zh: “错误再认”封闭了潜能与实现之间的断裂，而对当下的记忆恰恰使这一断裂清晰聚焦。错误再认把一种官能等同于它全部对象化形式的总和，把一般过去重新吸收进时间的年代序列。然而，潜能与实现、语言与说出的词、劳动力与某项具体劳动之间始终存在的差距——我们在感受到二者同时存在并相互归属的同时，也会感受到这一差距——正是历史时间的生成基础。因此，“错误再认”遮蔽了经验的历史性。现实的时代错置使经验去历史化。也就是说，它诱发一种心境，使人们得出结论：历史如今已经耗尽，“从来没有任何新事物……每个时刻［都是］过去的重复”。

en: If everything has happened already, nothing is worth the trouble. Every action is just a copy, or, better, a
taken from a script that we cannot question. But what is it, concretely, that prescribes our script? What are these acts that we are always on the point of

repeating? How is the imperious past, to which we epigones must conform, articulated? There can be no answer to such questions. The gestures that we carry out are, indeed, imitations, but we would never be able to point to the original by which they are inspired. The identical type is ever-returning yet remains unknown to us. We are compelled to reproduce something, but it is something undefined, an I-don’t-know-what whose content we can only ascertain after having reproduced it. But how come we get the impression that we are subject to a nameless coercion by its elusive physiognomy? Its origin is to be found in none other than the present, its double character, its splitting into a potential ‘now’ and an actual ‘now’.
zh: 如果一切都已经发生，就没有任何事情值得费力去做。每项行动都只是摹本；更确切地说，都是从一份我们无权质疑的剧本中取出的引文。但具体说来，究竟是什么规定了我们的剧本？我们仿佛总在重复的那些实现又是什么？我们这些后来者必须服从的那个强势过去，究竟如何组织起来？这些问题不可能得到回答。我们的举动确实是模仿，但我们永远无法指出它们所仿效的原本。那个相同类型不断返回，却始终不为我们所知。我们被迫复制某个东西，但它没有明确内容，只是一个不可名状的某物；只有在完成复制之后，我们才能确定它的内容。可是，它那难以捉摸的面貌，为什么会使我们觉得自己受到一种无名强制的支配？这种感觉的根源不是别的，正是当下本身，是当下的双重性质，是它分裂为潜在的“现在”和现实的“现在”。

en: ‘False recognition’ is, in a word,
. Everyday experience seems to reiterate a past, already-lived experience with philological scruple. It only
to do so, however: the previous event, despite having risen to the rank of an archetype, has in fact never taken place. Rather, it is the potential inherent within this

that is taking on the appearance of an earlier act, the act that seems despotically to demand its own repetition. And this is the reason why we can never specify what the ever-returning identical type is. The

contained within the present lords it over us like a peremptory fate or obscure precedent. History is stopped in its tracks, as our faculties are reduced to a script to which we must conform down to the last detail – a jumble of performances that must be reiterated
. We become epigones or spectators, but

children: epigones or spectators of our very own potential-to-be

zh: 一言以蔽之，“错误再认”之所以得名，就因为它是错误的。日常经验仿佛以考据学般的一丝不苟重演一段过去已经经历过的经验；但它仅仅是仿佛如此。那件先前事件尽管被提升到原型的地位，事实上却从未发生。真正发生的是：内在于此时此地的潜能采取了某项较早实现的外观，而那项较早实现仿佛专横地要求当前事件把它再现出来。这也正是我们永远无法明确说出那个不断返回的相同类型究竟是什么的原因。当下所包含的可能，以一道不容置疑的命运或一个晦暗先例的姿态支配着我们。历史被迫中途停步，因为我们的官能被还原成一份我们必须在每个细节上照办的剧本——一堆必须无限重复的实际表现。我们成了后来者或观众，但我们所追随、所观看的，其实正是我们自身能够存在的潜能。

现实的时代错置把形式的时代错置颠倒过来；这在某些方面或许类似康德称为“纯粹理性的谬误推理”（paralogisms of pure reason）的那种颇为隐蔽的误解。谬误推理把一个先天范畴（例如实体范畴）当成已经认识的内容（于是断言所有范畴——包括实体范畴——所依赖的纯粹自我本身就是……一个实体）。这样，我们便把使经验、使现象得以发生并得到表象的东西，误认作经验中现象的一项规定。同样，在我们的例子中，现实的时代错置把过去形式等同于过去事实，把语言等同于一段已经说出的言语，等等。因此可以说，现实的时代错置是记忆（以及历史理性）的谬误推理。
en: The
anachronism turning the
anachronism on its head perhaps in some senses resembles the rather insidious type of misunderstandings which Kant calls ‘paralogisms of pure reason’. The paralogism consists in taking an

category (the category of substance, for instance) for a known content (thus affirming that the pure Id on which all categories depend, including that of substance, is itself … a substance). Thus we exchange the thing that allows for experience – for phenomena to happen and be represented – for a determination of the phenomena experienced. In the same sense, in our example, the real anachronism equates the past-form to a past-fact, language into an already-uttered utterance, and so on. We could thus say that the real anachronism is the
(and of historical reason).
